title: Hugging Face models can now load on a TPU with one device setting
friendlyTitle: Hugging Face models can now run on a Google TPU without a rewrite
summary: Google has open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for its Tensor Processing Units, and Hugging Face says Transformers, Diffusers, and its Kernels library now run on it without a port to JAX or the older torch_xla path. Loading a language model is a device setting of tpu. An image pipeline is a move onto the same device. Hugging Face says its older Optimum TPU package is no longer required for those libraries, and that 96.5% of the Transformers tests that run on TPU currently pass.
friendlySummary: Google has open-sourced TorchTPU, software that lets ordinary PyTorch code run on Google's TPU chips. Hugging Face says its main model libraries, including Transformers and Diffusers, now work on that software. You no longer have to rewrite the model for JAX, or use the older torch_xla path. Loading a language model means setting the device to tpu. An image pipeline moves onto the same device. Hugging Face says 96.5% of the Transformers tests that run on a TPU currently pass.
whyItMatters: If you already have TPU capacity and a PyTorch model, the job no longer starts with a rewrite. It still requires a TPU, and the first compiled run is slower while the graph is built. The practical change is that a Hub model can target the chip the same way it targets a GPU.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If you already have TPU machines and a PyTorch model, you can try the chip without first rewriting the code. You still need a TPU, and the first compiled run is slower while the software builds a plan. The useful change is that a model from the Hub can target the chip the same way it targets a GPU.
